title: CRISPR screens decode cancer cell pathways that trigger γδ T cell detection
model: Daudi-Cas9 Burkitt lymphoma cells, genome-wide knockout library (90,709 guides, no non-targeting controls)
contrast: BTN3A-low vs BTN3A-high FACS sort, paired across 3 replicate infections (3 vs 3)
paper_calls: 497 genes enriched in BTN3A-low (pos) and 754 in BTN3A-high (neg) at FDR 0.10; BTN3A1/ECSIT/FBXW7/SPIB/IRF1/NLRC5 top positive, CTBP1/ZNF217/RUNX1 top negative
barcs_calls: 3,244 genes at FDR 0.10 on the paired low-vs-high term (1,350 up in low, 1,894 up in high); no control guides for a control null
named_hits: 8/8 positive regulators at FDR 0.10 (BTN3A1 #1, IRF1 #2, NLRC5 #3, SPIB #4, IRF8 #6, BTN3A2 #7, FBXW7 #8, ECSIT #9); negative regulators CTBP1 #1, RING1 #4, ZNF217 #3, RUNX1 #13 all recovered
verdict: BARCS reproduces the paper's BTN3A regulators almost exactly (top positive and negative hits match, rank correlation 0.76/0.75, ~494/497 and ~748/754 of the paper's calls recovered) on the companion FACS screen to GSE192828; calibration could not be checked because the library has no control guides.
